## Holding One Idea per Note Lets Each Idea Be Linked, Contested and Reused on Its Own

A main note that holds exactly one idea lets that idea be linked, contested and reused without bringing unrelated ideas with it. This is the atomicity principle. ^claim

### Scope & Conditions

- Applies to main (permanent) notes. Fleeting and literature notes are exempt, because they are temporary or shaped by their source.
- One idea is a unit of meaning, not a length limit. The right level is a judgement about what is useful for the task.
- A claim that needs a but or a however is a prompt to check for a second idea.

### Evidence

> "Write exactly one note for each idea and write as if you were writing for someone else"
> (Ahrens 2022, ch. 2, PDF p. 37) · [open in Calibre](calibre://view-book/GCcalibreBooks/704/EPUB?open_at=toc:2%20Everything%20You%20Need%20to%20Do)

> "The more "atomic" an idea, the more broadly you can employ it. The more complex an idea, the less surface area it has to be connected to others."
> (Doto 2024, "Part 2", PDF p. 78) · [open in Calibre](calibre://view-book/GCcalibreBooks/1491/EPUB?open_at=toc:Part%202)

The first quotation states the practice and the second supports the linking and reuse benefit. The step to contesting an idea on its own is my own reasoning, since an objection to a bundled note does not say which idea it targets.

### Implications

- A note that answers two questions should be split, so each answer can be linked to and disputed separately.
- An existing note can be linked or embedded instead of restated.
- A long note is a reason to check for a second idea, and is not proof of one.

### Falsifier

- Take a set of ideas written both as single-idea notes and as bundled notes. If the single-idea versions are not linked, challenged or reused more precisely over time, the claim is wrong.

### Related

- [[A Complex Note Has Little Surface Area to Connect While a Single Idea Can Link Across Topics]]—extends: explains why a single idea connects further.
- [[Linking as a Redundancy Reduction Strategy in Zettelkasten]]—shared mechanism: one canonical note per idea, linked from elsewhere.
- [[Proposition-Centred Notes Create Cognitive Leverage That Topical Notes Lack]]—extends: the single idea is most useful when it is an arguable claim.
- [[Atomic Enough Means the Fewest Pieces Necessary to Be Useful for the Task]]—extends: how small one idea should be is a judgement.
- [[The Words But and However Signal That What Follows May Deserve Its Own Note]]—extends: a drafting test for a second idea.

### Tensions

- [[The Notes of Luhmann Were Atomic-ish, Concise but Not Constrained]]—tension, not contradiction: the method worked for Luhmann without strict atomicity, so the benefit may be a matter of degree.

### See Also

- [[SoT - Atomic Note Standard (The Proposition Card)]]

### Further Reading

- Ahrens, Sönke. 2022. *How to Take Smart Notes: One Simple Technique to Boost Writing, Learning and Thinking*. Sönke Ahrens. [Open in Calibre](calibre://view-book/GCcalibreBooks/704/EPUB)—_corroborates the one-note-per-idea practice._

## {NEW}

PKM notes written in a personal first-person voice, with the questions and feelings left in, keep the thinking behind each conclusion visible to the writer later. An academic register tends to strip that out and leave only the result. ^claim

### Scope & Conditions

- Applies to notes that record your own thinking, such as journals, workbench notes and the commentary around an idea.
- It does not require feelings in every note. A claim card can state its proposition plainly and keep the voice for scope, doubts and reasons.
- Practical forms are writing as I, keeping unanswered questions, and recording reactions such as confusion or surprise.
- Voice is a different test from own words. Own words checks comprehension, while voice keeps the path by which you got there.

### Evidence

> "This is the personal connection that every reader wants to make with a writer; if we care about the writer we'll follow him into subjects that we could have sworn we never wanted to know about."
> (Zinsser and Zinsser 1988, ch. 7, PDF p. 97) · [open in Calibre](calibre://view-book/GCcalibreBooks/747/EPUB)

> "Such humanity is so rare in the prose of academics that it glitters when it appears"
> (Zinsser and Zinsser 1988, ch. 10, PDF p. 151) · [open in Calibre](calibre://view-book/GCcalibreBooks/747/EPUB)

Zinsser is writing about prose for other readers, so these quotations support only the value of a human voice. The claim that a personal voice keeps your own reasoning visible in private notes is my own reasoning.

[extends:: [[Personal Context and Relevance are Key to Knowledge Formation]], strength=4, confidence=high]

[depends_on:: [[SoT - Unified Writing to Think Process]], strength=3, confidence=medium]

### Implications

- Keep the question that prompted a note, even before it has an answer.
- Record doubt or surprise when it explains why the idea mattered.
- A note collection written this way is a record of discovery as well as a store of results.

### Falsifier

- Return after some months to matched notes written in a personal and in an impersonal register. If you reconstruct the reasoning no better from the personal ones, the claim is wrong.

### Related

- [[MOC - PKM as Process vs Product]]—part of: this is the method that hub names for working process first.
- [[Personal Context and Relevance are Key to Knowledge Formation]]—extends: voice is one way to attach information to your own context.
- [[SoT - Unified Writing to Think Process]]—depends on: voice matters because the writing is doing the thinking.
- [[Writing in Own Words Distinguishes Comprehension from the Illusion of Knowledge]]—similar but different: that note tests comprehension, this one preserves the path of thought.
- [[Writing puts us in the powerful position of being able to observe our thinking]]—complements: a visible train of thought is something you can observe.

### Tensions

- [[A Note Should Be Written So It Can Be Understood Out of Context]]—tension, not contradiction: that note writes for a reader without your context, so private shorthand and unexplained feelings can defeat it.

- Zinsser, William, and William Knowlton Zinsser. 1988. *Writing to Learn*. Harper & Row. [Open in Calibre](calibre://view-book/GCcalibreBooks/747/EPUB)—_corroborates the value of a human voice, in writing for others rather than private notes._

- Applies when a task involves more items than working memory can hold at once. A trivial task gains little.

## Identity Integration Shifts Habit Execution From Doing to Being

Framing a repeated behaviour as part of who you are ("I am a runner"), rather than as a task you perform ("I am going for a run"), makes it easier to sustain. Each repetition then confirms a chosen self-concept instead of being negotiated from scratch. ^claim

### Scope & Conditions

- Applies to repeated behaviours that a person has chosen and values. A one-off action gives an identity nothing to build on.
- The identity needs to rest on observable actions. A label with no repetitions behind it is only an aspiration.
- It should be defined by showing up, not by flawless performance. Binding self-worth to an unbroken streak can backfire when normal capacity limits interrupt it.

### Evidence

> "Every action you take is a vote for the type of person you wish to become."
> (Clear 2018, ch. 2, PDF p. 41) · [open in Calibre]({two})

> "The ultimate form of intrinsic motivation is when a habit becomes part of your identity."
> (Clear 2018, ch. 2, PDF p. 38) · [open in Calibre]({two})

Clear states the mechanism in a practitioner book, and these quotations are assertions rather than a test of it. This claim is also point 8 of the 9-Point Consistency Framework in [[SoT - Intentional Living]].

[supports:: [[Consistency Depends on Structural Design Rather Than Willpower]], strength=4, confidence=medium]

### Implications

- Small repetitions count, because each one is evidence for the identity even when volume is minimal.
- Choose the identity by values first, then pick the smallest action that expresses it.
- Pair the framing with compassionate setback recovery, so a missed day does not read as a verdict on the self.

### Falsifier

- Compare people building the same habit with identity framing and with task or outcome framing. If adherence after several months is no better, or lapses lead to abandonment more often, the claim is wrong.

### Steelman

> "The tighter we cling to an identity, the harder it becomes to grow beyond it."
> (Clear 2018, ch. 20, PDF p. 203) · [open in Calibre]({c}20:%20The%20Downside%20of%20Creating%20Good%20Habits)

The strongest objection is that the same fusion which sustains a habit makes it costly to change or to miss. A person who cannot run may then lose a sense of self as well as an activity.

### Related

- [[Consistency Depends on Structural Design Rather Than Willpower]]—supports: identity framing is one anchor of consistency that does not rely on momentary motivation.
- [[Intentionality]]—depends on: the identity worth repeating is chosen from your values.
- [[SoT - Intentional Living]]—part of: section 4.8 of the intentional living framework.
- [[SoT - Habit Formation Framework]]—extends: places identity at the core of a wider method for building habits.
- [[Reframe Habit Setbacks as Capacity Limits Not Character Flaws]]—complements: protects the identity when a repetition is missed.

### Tensions

- [[Claim - When intelligence is bound to identity, epistemic errors are experienced as threats to self-worth]]—tension, not contradiction: fusing identity with a trait turns failure into a threat, whereas this claim relies on fusion with a repeatable action.

### Further Reading

- Clear, James. 2018. *Atomic Habits*. Penguin Random House. [Open in Calibre](calibre://view-book/GCcalibreBooks/690/EPUB)—_corroborates the mechanism and states its downside._
'''

- Applies to the structure of a whole note-taking system, such as its folders, categories and rules.

### Scope & Conditions

- Applies to patterns over weeks and across activities, so one flat or excited day settles nothing.

## {NEW}

Treating plans, self-images and circumstances as temporary makes it easier to adapt when they change than trying to hold them fixed. Zen practice trains this by accepting that everything, including oneself, is always changing. ^claim

### Scope & Conditions

- Applies to things that will change whatever you do, and to the form that valued things take over time.
- Accepting a change is not approving of it or giving up on influencing what happens next.
- Commitments and values can still be held steady while the plans that serve them are revised.

### Evidence

> "if we can accept this impermanence and embrace it, life becomes less of a struggle."
> (Babauta 2023, "Seeing and Working with True Nature", PDF p. 82) · [open in Calibre]({u}?open_at=toc:Seeing%20and%20Working%20with%20True%20Nature)

> "Instead of resisting the impermanence, if we can accept and embrace it, let go of our ideal of what we want life to be, perhaps we’ll struggle less."
> (Babauta 2023, "How to cope with loss", PDF p. 86) · [open in Calibre]({u}?open_at=toc:How%20to%20cope%20with%20loss)

Babauta, writing for a general reader about Zen practice, supports less struggle, and does so tentatively in the second passage. The step from less struggle to easier adaptation is my own reasoning.

### Implications

- Write plans and routines expecting to revise them, and treat a revision as normal rather than as failure.
- Hold a self-description loosely enough that new evidence can change it.
- When a change causes distress, ask which earlier state you are still trying to keep.

### Falsifier

- Compare how people who expect revision and people who expect stability cope with the same disrupted plan. If the first group does not resume useful action sooner or report less distress, the claim is wrong.

### Steelman

Expecting everything to change can weaken the effort to protect what is worth keeping. A person who accepts too readily may adapt to a bad situation that could have been resisted.

### Related

- [[The Four Noble Truths Explain Suffering from Attachment]]—depends on: the account of why holding on to what changes causes distress.
- [[Letting Go of Fixed Views Leads to Peace]]—similar: applies the same release to how people and the world ought to be.
- [[Morita Therapy - Arugamama is Accepting Reality As It Is]]—complements: acceptance frees energy for constructive action.
- [[SoT - Wabi-Sabi]]—extends: finds value in what is transient and unfinished.
- [[Zen Defines Enlightenment as a Process Not a Destination]]—applies: even clarity is treated as passing and not as a state to keep.
- [[MOC - Why Chasing Enlightenment Causes Suffering]]—part of: the hub that uses impermanence to explain that paradox.

## {NEW}

Filing a note by the situations in which you want to meet it again produces more useful connections than filing it by the topic it belongs to. The first is how a writer thinks, and the second is how an archivist thinks. ^claim

### Scope & Conditions

- Applies to notes meant to develop ideas and feed writing or decisions.
- A reference collection kept for known lookups may be better served by topic filing.
- It needs some idea of your current questions and interests, because they define the situations to file for.

### Evidence

> "In the old system, the question is: Under which topic do I store this note? In the new system, the question is: In which context will I want to stumble upon it again?"
> {c(6,63,"6 Simplicity Is Paramount")}

> "The archivist asks: Which keyword is the most fitting? A writer asks: In which circumstances will I want to stumble upon this note, even if I forget about it?"
> {c(12,144,"12 Develop Ideas")}

Ahrens sets out the contrast and argues for the second question. The comparative claim about the number of useful connections is my own reasoning from that argument, and these quotations do not measure it.

### Implications

- When saving a note, name a question or project in which meeting it would help.
- Choose links and keywords with that situation in mind, not by looking at the note alone.
- Ask where a note will be useful before asking where it belongs.

### Falsifier

- File matched sets of notes by topic and by situation of reuse. If after some months the second set has not produced more connections that get used, the claim is wrong.

### Related

- [[Concept-Orientation Enables Cross-Domain Discovery]]—shared mechanism: filing by idea and not by source also lets connections cross domains.
- [[A Simple Note-Taking Structure Lets Complexity Build Up at the Content Level]]—shared mechanism: both reject sorting notes into topic hierarchies.
- [[Bottom-Up Organization Allows Emergent Structure]]—complements: topics can emerge from links instead of being decided first.
- [[Creating Meaningful Links]]—extends: the situation of reuse gives a reason for a link.
- [[Stage 4 Connect (The Zettelkasten Layer)]]—part of: this is the question to ask at the connecting stage.

### Tensions

- [[Hub Notes Provide Entry Points to Idea Clusters]]—tension, not contradiction: hubs gather notes around a topic or question, which helps entry once a cluster exists.

### Further Reading

- Ahrens, Sönke. 2022. *How to Take Smart Notes: One Simple Technique to Boost Writing, Learning and Thinking*. Sönke Ahrens. [Open in Calibre](calibre://view-book/GCcalibreBooks/704/EPUB)—_corroborates the contrast between the two questions._

## {NEW}

Treating a virtue such as compassion or mindfulness as something you do in each action, rather than as something you are, makes it easier to resume after a lapse. A lapse is then one missed action and not proof that you lack the quality. ^claim

### Scope & Conditions

- Applies to qualities that can be acted out again soon, such as patience, attention or compassion.
- It does not excuse the lapse. Repair may still be owed to the people affected.
- Zen is the background. The old version of this note credited the teaching of enlightened activity over enlightened people to Suzuki Roshi, which I have not verified.

### Evidence

> "The skill to practice is to get back on track if you mess up, and to not let it derail you."
> {{Q1}}

Babauta treats recovery as a skill to practise. The quotation does not compare doing with being, so the claim that the framing makes recovery easier is my own reasoning and is a hypothesis.

### Implications

- After a lapse, name the next action that expresses the quality and do it.
- State household or work standards as actions that can be seen and repeated.
- Avoid asking whether you are a patient person when the useful question is what a patient act is now.

### Falsifier

- Compare how soon people resume after a lapse when the same standard is framed as an action and as an identity. If the action framing brings no quicker or more frequent return, the claim is wrong.

### Related

- [[Zen Defines Enlightenment as a Process Not a Destination]]—depends on: enlightenment as passing moments leaves no permanent status to hold.
- [[Chasing Enlightenment as a Goal Causes Suffering]]—complements: describes the cost of pursuing the status itself.
- [[The Four Noble Truths Explain Suffering from Attachment]]—extends: a self-image can be one more thing held on to.
- [[MOC - Why Chasing Enlightenment Causes Suffering]]—part of: the hub in which action is the answer to that paradox.
- [[Reframe Habit Setbacks as Capacity Limits Not Character Flaws]]—shared mechanism: a setback is read as an event and not as a verdict on character.
- [[Respect Is a Set of Agreed Actions and Not an Identity]]—similar: defines a quality by actions in a household.

### Tensions

- [[Identity Integration Shifts Habit Execution From Doing to Being]]—tension: that claim says framing a behaviour as who you are sustains it, while this one says that framing it as what you do aids recovery.

### Further Reading

- Babauta, Leo. 2023. *Essential Zen Habits: Mastering the Art of Change Briefly*. Waking Lion Press. [Open in Calibre](calibre://view-book/GCcalibreBooks/741/EPUB)—_corroborates the value of recovering after a lapse without testing this framing._
